paragraphs.en: The journal Science is adding an extra round of statistical checks to its peer-review process, editor-in-chief Marcia McNutt announced today. The policy follows similar efforts from other journals, after widespread concern that basic mistakes in data analysis are contributing to the irreproducibility of many published research findings.
paragraphs.zh: 《科学》杂志主编玛西娅·麦克纳特今天宣布，该刊将在同行评审流程中增加一轮统计审查。此前，数据分析中的基本错误正在导致许多已发表研究成果无法复现的问题，引起了广泛关注，其他期刊也采取了类似措施，这项政策正是对这些努力的跟进。

paragraphs.en: “Readers must have confidence in the conclusions published in our journal,” writes McNutt in an editorial. Working with the American Statistical Association, the journal has appointed seven experts to a statistics board of reviewing editors (SBoRE). Manuscripts will be flagged up for additional scrutiny by the journal’s internal editors, or by its existing Board of Reviewing Editors or by outside peer reviewers. The SBoRE panel will then find external statisticians to review these manuscripts.
paragraphs.zh: 麦克纳特在一篇社论中写道：“读者必须能够信赖本刊发表的结论。”该刊与美国统计学会合作，任命了七名专家组成统计审稿编辑委员会（SBoRE）。杂志内部编辑、现有审稿编辑委员会或外部同行评审者，将标记出需要进一步审查的稿件。随后，统计审稿编辑委员会将寻找外部统计学家，对这些稿件进行评审。

paragraphs.en: Asked whether any particular papers had impelled the change, McNutt said: “The creation of the ‘statistics board’ was motivated by concerns broadly with the application of statistics and data analysis in scientific research and is part of Science’s overall drive to increase reproducibility in the research we publish.”
paragraphs.zh: 当被问及是否有某些特定论文促成了这一改变时，麦克纳特说：“设立‘统计委员会’，源于我们对科学研究中统计学和数据分析应用的普遍关切，也是《科学》为提高所刊载研究的可重复性而开展的整体工作的一部分。”

paragraphs.en: Giovanni Parmigiani, a biostatistician at the Harvard School of Public Health, a member of the SBoRE group, says he expects the board to “play primarily an advisory role.” He agreed to join because he “found the foresight behind the establishment of the SBoRE to be novel, unique and likely to have a lasting impact. This impact will not only be through the publications in Science itself, but hopefully through a larger group of publishing places that may want to model their approach after Science.”
paragraphs.zh: 哈佛大学公共卫生学院生物统计学家、统计审稿编辑委员会成员乔瓦尼·帕尔米贾尼表示，他希望该委员会“主要发挥咨询作用”。他同意加入，是因为他“认为设立这一委员会所体现的远见新颖而独特，并可能产生持久影响。这种影响不仅会通过《科学》本身发表的论文体现出来，还有望通过更多出版平台发挥作用，因为这些平台可能愿意仿效《科学》的做法。”

paragraphs.en: John Ioannidis, a physician who studies research methodology, says that the policy is “a most welcome step forward” and “long overdue”. “Most journals are weak in statistical review, and this damages the quality of what they publish. I think that, for the majority of scientific papers nowadays, statistical review is more essential than expert review,” he says, but he noted that biomedical journals such as Annals of Internal Medicine, the Journal of the American Medical Association and The Lancet pay strong attention to statistical review.
paragraphs.zh: 研究科研方法的医生约翰·约安尼迪斯表示，这项政策是“极为可喜的进步”，而且“早就该出台了”。他说：“大多数期刊的统计审查薄弱，这损害了其发表内容的质量。我认为，对当今大多数科学论文而言，统计审查比专家评审更为重要。”但他也指出，《内科学年鉴》《美国医学会杂志》和《柳叶刀》等生物医学期刊十分重视统计审查。

paragraphs.en: Professional scientists are expected to know how to analyse data, but statistical errors are alarmingly common in published research, according to David Vaux, a cell biologist. Researchers should improve their standards, he wrote in 2012, but journals should also take a tougher line, “engaging reviewers who are statistically literate and editors who can verify the process”. Vaux says that Science’s idea to pass some papers to statisticians “has some merit, but a weakness is that it relies on the board of reviewing editors to identify ‘the papers that need scrutiny’ in the first place”.
paragraphs.zh: 细胞生物学家戴维·沃克斯表示，专业科学家理应懂得如何分析数据，但已发表研究中统计错误之普遍，令人震惊。他在2012年写道，研究人员应提高自身标准，而期刊也应采取更严格的态度，“聘请具备统计素养的审稿人，以及能够核查分析过程的编辑”。沃克斯说，《科学》把一些论文交给统计学家审查的想法“有一定可取之处，但其弱点在于，它首先依赖审稿编辑委员会去识别‘需要仔细审查的论文’。”
